texts: good. the lighting, Coraline Ash, the Harbor Station's lantern, sundown and the day-100/Year-1 date are all covered. One standing caveat, not a fault of this sentence: the engine orders dates by year/month/day, so a day-of-year date with no month is stored but is not comparable with another day — only explicit sequencing wording ('the following day', 'after the ...') produces an ordering.
good. the lantern is the burner and the mire-essence the consumed thing, and the mire-essence gets its own symbol so the later definite mentions link back to it.
good. 'in the lantern' correctly attaches to the mire-essence itself rather than to the holding, and the holding of salt-bloom sits on that same mire-essence symbol.

mixed: the sentence parses on its own (a burning undergone by the mire-essence, manner 'slowly'), but it mints a SECOND burning with no link back to the lantern's burning two sentences earlier and with no burner named at all, so 'slowly' never attaches to the burning the passage is about. Either fold the manner into the earlier clause — 'The lantern burned mire-essence slowly.' — or restate the participants here: 'The lantern burned the mire-essence slowly.'
good. producing mist-light comes out as a creation event with the lantern as the producer, and mist-light is typed and linked to 'light'.
good. the moths become one group that the later sentences reuse, and 'attracted' correctly leaves them unchanged.
good. the group landing is recorded and a fireable per-moth rule hands the landing to any individual moth named later.

bad: the threads are given the 'changed object' role, which claims the moths created or altered them, whereas the sentence only says the threads ended up on the lantern — and the same wrong role is copied into the per-moth rule. Rewrite with a plain placement verb: 'The nightmoths deposited silken threads on the lantern.' If the moths really do produce the silk there, say that instead and the create-reading becomes correct: 'The nightmoths spun silken threads on the lantern.'
good. the collecting, the threads, the lantern as the source, and dawn / day 101 / Year 1 are all covered.
good. the carrying, the threads and Cauldron Hall as the destination are all covered, and the hall is typed from its own name.

mixed: the two stacked 'in' phrases both flatten onto the boiling as coordinate locations, so the parse says the boiling was in sea-water and, separately, in the third cauldron, with nothing recording that the sea-water was in the cauldron. Give the medium its own role instead: 'Hesper boiled the silken threads with sea-water in the third cauldron on day 101 of Year 1.' — 'with' makes the sea-water the means used and leaves the cauldron as the single location.
good. the forming is placed in the third cauldron (the same cauldron as the previous sentence) and 'by evening' is recorded as a deadline rather than as an exact time.
good. the storing, the clay vessel and its 'vessel' genus are all covered, and the location rides the storing event only, so nothing claims where the essence sits afterwards.
good. 'the stored mire-essence' resolves to the very essence Hesper stored, and sundown / day 101 / Year 1 are carried on the drawing.
